ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Joe Louis

code.originalText: Fifteen-week review off the antipsychotic: recovery, blood pressure and finances

text.paragraph: Mr. Louis returns five weeks after his ten-week review. He finished the aripiprazole taper three weeks ago and has had no persecutory thoughts and no trouble sleeping. He completed twelve weeks of contingency management: 22 of 24 scheduled tests were done and 21 were negative, the positive one after his single day of use; he has had no cocaine since. On his trip last month he tested at a partner clinic and had his therapy session by phone. He will continue weekly therapy and a weekly urine test for now. His home readings average 124/78 mmHg. The tax clinic reviewed his records and found nothing owed; with the social worker he has a budget and has applied for veterans' health benefits. He would like his zoster and second hepatitis B vaccines today. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-26; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 126/78, pulse 72; weight 101.6 kg, BMI 29.1
Regular rhythm; no murmur; no edema

Persecutory thoughts and poor sleep for about two months: a fixed belief that people are following him and plan to harm him, three to four hours of sleep a night, partial insight; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented fears of a plot against his life; resolved into the diagnosis at the consultation. Not a claim about his real symptoms.
Cocaine use disorder, severe (seven of eleven DSM-5-TR criteria): intranasal cocaine most days for about a year, last use three days before intake
S — Synthetic modern coding at intake; superseded at the consultation by the combined code once the psychotic disorder was diagnosed. Person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.

Cocaine use disorder, severe, with cocaine-induced psychotic disorder (persecutory delusions during heavy use, persisting ten days after the last use, with no history of psychosis off cocaine, a normal examination and no evidence of a neurocognitive disorder); psychotic symptoms resolved within four weeks on aripiprazole
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation. Not a claim about his real diagnosis.
Raised blood pressure at intake (154/98 mmHg) three days after cocaine use, without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings planned
S — Synthetic presenting finding; resolved into a diagnosis of hypertension at four weeks.

Hypertension, stage 2, confirmed four weeks after the last cocaine use (clinic 146/92, home average 144/90 mmHg), with mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy and a normal aortic root on echocardiography; treated with amlodipine
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the four-week visit.
Financial insecurity: years of tax debt from his time as a well-paid athlete, now settled, left him with no savings; irregular income from paid appearances; worry about money keeps him awake
S — Synthetic social need anchored to his documented tax debt.
Acute viral upper respiratory infection (common cold) for three days; rapid tests negative for influenza and COVID-19; resolved within ten days without antibiotics
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

Cocaine use disorder, severe, with cocaine-induced psychotic disorder, psychosis in remission off treatment (F14.250). No psychotic symptoms three weeks after stopping aripiprazole and eight weeks without cocaine. A return of psychosis would most likely follow renewed cocaine use, and he knows the warning signs. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone. [S]
Weekly therapy and weekly urine tests for three more months.
Restart treatment early if persecutory thoughts or sleeplessness return.
Keep naloxone and test strips at home.

Continue amlodipine 5 mg.

Follow-up: Zoster vaccine and second hepatitis B dose given today. Review in three months; second zoster dose in two to six months; second hepatitis A dose in four months. Weekly therapy and urine tests. Call the clinic or 988 at any time. [S]
